grammarSchedule.why: `did`/`didn't` need no concept - `did` is English glue and `not` is A1 - and A1 supplies the lexical verbs (`to go`, `to see`), so `Did you go?` / `I didn't see him` are writable at once
`to be` and `when` are A1; lesson 1 adds `while`, so `I was reading while she was cooking` works from the first lesson
`to have` and `never` are A1; lesson 3 adds `already` and `still`, which sharpen the unfinished-time contrast, but `I have never been to London` is writable at lesson 1
what/where/when/who/why/how are all A1 and `do`/`does` is glue, so no A2 word is needed
`do`/`does` is glue and A1 has the lexical verbs, so `Do you like pizza?` needs nothing from this level
a tag is only `to be`/`to do` plus `not` plus an A1 pronoun; `It's cold today, isn't it?` is writable immediately
`to know` and every wh-word are A1, `do` is glue: `Do you know where the station is?` needs only the A1 pool
a bare base verb plus `don't` (glue `do` + A1 `not`) covers instruction and prohibition. `let's` cannot be written: there is no `let` row anywhere in the bank

BLOCKED: there is no `could` row in the bank at any level. Lesson 2 is where it belongs, next to `would`, `might` and `shall`; until the bank gets a `could` row this topic cannot be demonstrated at all - `can` (A1) is a different form and fails the test
`must` is A1 and `not` is A1, so `You must wear a seatbelt` / `You mustn't smoke here` need nothing new
`to have` is A1 and `to` is glue, so `have[to have] to work[to work]` is legal without a new row
`should` is A1; `You should see a doctor` is writable at once, and lesson 29 adds `doctor`-adjacent vocabulary for richer advice
`might` is taught in lesson 2. The modal `may` does not exist as a concept (the bank's `may` is the month, German `der Mai`), so every sentence for this topic must use `might`
`shall` is taught in lesson 2, and `to open`, `to go`, `to help` are A1, so `Shall I open the window?` works from lesson 2
`can` is A1, and permission is a use of it rather than a new word: `Can I use your phone?` is writable at lesson 1. The missing modal `may` does not block this topic
`to be` and `to go` are A1 and `to` is glue, so `going[to go] to visit[to visit]` needs no new row
`to be`, `tomorrow` and `next` are A1; lesson 3 adds `soon` and lesson 11 `to meet`, but the pattern is writable at lesson 1
`will` and `not` are A1 (won't, will you...?), and `shall` arrives in lesson 2, which is what the shall half of the topic waits for
`will` and `to be` are A1, so `I'll be waiting for you` is writable at lesson 1; lesson 13 adds `to wait` for the stock example
`if` is taught in lesson 1 and both clauses are present simple or an imperative, both of which the A1 pool supports
`to be` and `by` are A1 and the participle is a form of an A1 verb, so `The letter was sent` works once lesson 19 adds `to send`; the pattern itself is writable at lesson 1 with A1 verbs
`to say` and `to tell` are A1 and lesson 1 teaches `that (conjunction)`, so `She said that she was tired` is writable at lesson 1
`who`, `which` and `that` are all A1, so a defining clause needs no A2 word

PARTLY BLOCKED: `more` and every short adjective are A1, so `This film is more interesting` is writable, but there is no `than` row anywhere in the bank, so the second half of the comparison cannot be written until one is added
`the` is glue and `most` is A1, so `the biggest city` / `the most expensive hotel` work at lesson 1; lesson 86 adds `the best` for the fixed form
`water`, `money`, `food`, `some` and `any` are all A1; lesson 39 adds `music` for the stock example
`all`, `both`, `each`, `much` and `many` are A1, so `I don't have much money` works at lesson 1. `a few` is a B1 row and cannot be used at this level
this/that/these/those are A1; referring back is a use of them, not a new word
`'s` is glue and A1 supplies the nouns, so `Anna's book` / `the students' books` need nothing new
`to turn off`, `to get up`, `to put on` and `to look for` are already A1; lesson 103 adds `tidy up`, lesson 163 `pick up` and lesson 177 `call up` for more range
`to enjoy` is taught in lesson 18; `would` (lesson 2) plus A1 `to love` gives the `would love to ...` half
PARTLY BLOCKED: `myself` is taught in lesson 7 and `oneself` is A1, but yourself/himself/herself/itself have no bank rows, so only first-person and generic reflexives can be written
someone/something/anyone/anything/nothing and `not` are all A1, so `I don't want anything` works at lesson 1; lesson 7 adds `nobody`, `nowhere` and `nothing at all` for the no-compound half
`what` is A1, `a` is glue and A1 supplies the adjectives, so `What a beautiful day!` is writable at lesson 1
`so` (German `also`, the summarizing marker) is taught in lesson 1; `as you know` has no row of its own but composes from A1 `as`, `you` and `to know`

lessons.theme: what people are like at work
